scope: Independent read-only audit of the sole prior CPU attempt. No worker, native API experiment, WSL, GPU, model, repair or retry was launched.

integrity.source_pin_limit: The seven source matches were observed at the mission base before the current diagnostic edits. This does not claim modified candidate bytes equal prior attempt pins.
integrity.disjoint_identity_limit: The observed sets do not establish causal isolation or identify the failing operation.

target.limit: One stdlib Windows fixture tree only; no model, GPU, WSL or full orchestrator qualification.

sentinel.cause: Unproven. The prior host error has no traceback, failing native API, access mask, affected PID, native last-error capture or error timestamp.

timeline_limits: Filesystem timestamps are corroborating metadata; their values are not part of the committed content hashes.
Resource observations include cleanup. The final resource sample is not the timestamp of the original exception.
The prior windows field was overwritten by each successful snapshot and final settlement; it is not a per-call or per-snapshot identity history.
Saved cumulative identities show membership when observed, not continued liveness at the failing operation.
No saved record identifies when host cleanup CANCEL was sent or received relative to sentinel natural finish.
Empty stage/bootstrap stderr cannot identify the host-side failing operation.
PowerShell JSON parsing may display date values in local timezone; the recorded UTC strings here were verified against raw JSON text.
source_findings: The originating error field is written by OwnedStageRunner.run's normal-phase exception handler. Cleanup failures have distinct fields.
The successful stage-started and readiness records exclude initial constructor, launch and attach as the original failing operation.
Prior OpenProcess failures were silently skipped and could not by themselves surface the saved PermissionError.
Prior IsProcessInJob native failure was converted to RuntimeError and therefore did not by itself yield the saved PermissionError.
Possible later host failures include checked Job/process queries, host memory/disk observation, protocol file operations, subprocess polling, host control pipe operations and transport-file close.
